definitions.gloss: waterfall meditation; waterfall ascetic practice; standing under a waterfall as spiritual training
definitions.explanation: A form of ascetic practice in which a person stands or sits under a waterfall, enduring the cold water as a means of spiritual purification and mental discipline. Rooted in Shinto and Buddhist traditions.

examples.japanese: {山寺|やまでら}で{滝行|たきぎょう}を{体験|たいけん}した。
examples.english: I experienced waterfall meditation at a mountain temple.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}の{滝行|たきぎょう}は{極|きわ}めて{過酷|かこく}だ。
examples.english: Waterfall meditation in winter is extremely harsh.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{観光客|かんこうきゃく}にも{滝行|たきぎょう}を{体験|たいけん}させてくれる{寺|てら}が{増|ふ}えており、{精神|せいしん}{修養|しゅうよう}の{一環|いっかん}として{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Recently, more temples are offering waterfall meditation experiences to tourists, and it is popular as a form of mental discipline.

notes:
Composed of {滝|たき} (waterfall) and {行|ぎょう} (ascetic practice; training). Part of the broader tradition of {修行|しゅぎょう} (ascetic training) in Japanese religion.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally practiced by Buddhist monks and {山伏|やまぶし} (mountain ascetics) as a form of {禊|みそぎ} (purification). The practitioner wears white clothing and chants sutras or prayers while standing under the waterfall. In recent years, some temples have opened {滝行|たきぎょう} to lay participants, making it a popular spiritual tourism activity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {滝行|たきぎょう}を{行|おこな}う: to perform waterfall meditation
- {滝行|たきぎょう}を{体験|たいけん}する: to experience waterfall meditation
- {滝行|たきぎょう}{体験|たいけん}: waterfall meditation experience (program)
- {滝行|たきぎょう}の{場所|ばしょ}: waterfall meditation site

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {修行|しゅぎょう}: ascetic training; religious practice — the general term for spiritual training, of which {滝行|たきぎょう} is one specific form
- {禊|みそぎ}: purification ritual — a Shinto cleansing practice, often involving cold water but not necessarily a waterfall
- {座禅|ざぜん}: seated Zen meditation — another form of spiritual practice, but done sitting rather than under water
